title: Microsoft Graph Change Notifications - Simply Explained
description:
Polling Microsoft Graph every few minutes wastes requests, misses changes and can get your app throttled. This episode explains for Microsoft 365 developers how change notifications, subscriptions, validation and renewal work, and how to build reliable real-time apps with delta queries as a safety net.
In this episode
00:00 – The problem with polling01:04 – What are change notifications?02:34 – Creating a subscription04:16 – The validation handshake05:16 – Subscription renewal06:26 – Reliability and safety nets08:08 – Real-world use cases09:26 – Choosing the delivery channel
Key takeaways
Microsoft Graph change notifications push events to your app through subscriptions, replacing wasteful polling that risks throttling.Every subscription needs a validation handshake within 10 seconds and must be renewed before its resource-specific expiration.Acknowledge notifications fast, use delta queries as a safety net, and choose webhooks, Event Hubs or Event Grid based on volume.
Worth quoting
“Change, notifications, let your app react instantly to events in Microsoft 365 without constant checking.” – Mirko Peters (01:08)
“It's a security check. It proves your endpoint is alive, listening, and under your control. It stops someone from pointing a subscription at a URL they don't own, hoping to intercept notifications meant for someone else.” – Mirko Peters (04:52)
